description: A set operation combines each operand's PROJECTED SELECT list, not the raw base rows, so a+1 UNION b is the union of the two computed columns and a UNION over one projected column de-duplicates on THAT column even though the rows differ elsewhere. INTERSECT binds TIGHTER than UNION and EXCEPT (Snowflake operator precedence), so 1 UNION 2 INTERSECT 2 is 1 UNION (2 INTERSECT 2) and answers both rows, not the single row the left-to-right reading would give. Mixed numeric types across branches - an integer column beside a decimal literal - must still SORT rather than fail on the mixed carriers. And FETCH applies to the COMBINED result. Converted 1:1 from query/SetOperationProjectionTest (now retired); the Java read cells by index, so each converted test pins the whole ordered row set.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sp (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
SELECT a+1 FROM sp UNION SELECT b FROM sp ORDER BY 1
CREATE TABLE sp2 (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
SELECT a FROM sp2 UNION SELECT a FROM sp2 ORDER BY 1
SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 2 INTERSECT SELECT 2 ORDER BY 1
CREATE TABLE sp (a INTEGER, b INTEGER)
SELECT a FROM sp EXCEPT SELECT 2
SELECT a FROM mn UNION SELECT 1.5 ORDER BY 1
SELECT a FROM sp3 UNION SELECT a FROM sp3 ORDER BY a FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS ONLY
